From action values to state values

In a state, the policy picks an action at random, and each action has its own expected return. So the state's value is an average of the action values, weighted by how often the policy picks each one.

Icy gridworld, $\gamma = 0.9$. Every cell follows the random policy except the one you select (blue). Drag its four sliders to change $\pi(\cdot \mid s)$ there. Cells show $v_\pi$.

Bars: $q_\pi(s, a)$ for the selected cell. Green number: $\pi(a \mid s)$. Amber dashes: $v_\pi(s)$.

The maths

Split the return by the first action. By the law of total expectation,

$$\begin{aligned} v_\pi(s) &= \mathbb{E}_\pi[G_t \mid S_t = s] \\ &= \sum_a \Pr\{A_t = a \mid S_t = s\} \\ &\qquad\quad \times \mathbb{E}_\pi[G_t \mid S_t = s, A_t = a] \\ &= \sum_a \pi(a \mid s)\, q_\pi(s, a) \end{aligned}$$

The state value is the average of the action values, weighted by the policy. No model of the ice is needed for this direction.

Because the weights are non-negative and add to 1, the average lies between the smallest and the largest action value:

$$\min_a q_\pi(s, a) \;\le\; v_\pi(s) \;\le\; \max_a q_\pi(s, a)$$

It reaches the top only when all the weight sits on the best actions. "All on the best" does that. For ε-greedy (Lesson 3) with one best action $a^*$,

$$v_\pi(s) = (1 - \varepsilon)\, q_\pi(s, a^*) + \frac{\varepsilon}{|\mathcal{A}|} \sum_a q_\pi(s, a)$$

One subtlety you can see in the bars: when you change $\pi$ in a cell, its own $q$ values move a little too. The agent can come back to that cell later, and then it acts with the new policy. The identity holds for every policy, because both sides are computed for the same $\pi$.
